convergence: Large-u power counting: the eps^n integrand is bounded by const * T^{-E+n} * (polynomial in beta, bounded); the region has E-1 non-compact directions (u_special in [0,1]) and T >= E-1 >= 1, so int T^{-E+n} converges for n <= 0 (int r^{E-2} r^{-E} dr = int r^-2 dr). Termwise: a monomial u^alpha T^{-(E-n+|alpha|)} converges iff E - n + |alpha| > (sum of the non-compact exponents) + E - 1, true for n <= 0 (asserted for every master integral used: J3 needs m > a2+a3+2, J2 needs m > a2+1).  Remainder: |e^{-x} - sum_{j<=J} (-x)^j/j!| <= C x^{J+1/2} for x >= 0 bounds the error of the eps^0 truncation by const * eps^{1/2} * int T^{-E+1/2} < oo; hence graph(eps) = eps^-1 g_{-1} + g_0 + o(1) exactly, with g_0 the order-omega Taylor coefficient.
